entries.title: Welcome
entries.body: The welcome screen introduces PseudoLearn, lets you choose the language and syntax profile and offers a guided step-by-step demo. It appears the first time you open the app.

entries.title: Library
entries.body: The Library gathers your algorithms and exercises in two tabs, each with its item count and its own “+” button to create. In “Algorithms”, search by title, open an algorithm to edit it, or use each card menu to rename or delete it. Algorithms are stored on the device and synced when you sign in.

entries.title: New algorithm
entries.body: “New algorithm” creates an empty document. You choose a unique title and the syntax profile: classic Spanish or English. The profile decides the program keywords and can be translated later.

entries.title: Exercises
entries.body: The “Exercises” tab lists the exercises you created and offers “New exercise”. “Solve” opens your attempt as an algorithm with the exercise strip; “Edit” opens the exercise editor and “Delete” removes it without deleting your attempts.

entries.title: Exercise editor
entries.body: The exercise editor defines the title, an optional story, the statement, restrictions, graded hints, visible and hidden cases (one line per case: inputs separated by semicolons, then => and the outputs), structural assertions and the reference solution. It is published only if the reference solution passes every case and assertion.

entries.title: Algorithm editor
entries.body: The editor analyses the program as you type and shows diagnostics with their explanation. From the bottom bar you run all at once or step by step, see the output, the variable trace, the flowchart, the structogram and the class diagram, and export equivalent Python or Rust code. The document saves itself.

entries.title: Run options
entries.body: Run options store with the document the arguments your program receives (separated by spaces; use quotes to include spaces), let you replay the last execution tape to reproduce exactly the same effects and show the files folder where the program reads and writes.

entries.title: Knowledge
entries.body: Knowledge gathers the learning route, with graded lessons and exercises, and the illustrated language specification. Your progress is marked on each lesson.

entries.title: Route lesson
entries.body: A lesson explains a concept with runnable examples, links to the specification and practice exercises. Opening it marks it «In progress»; it becomes «Completed» once you solve all its required exercises, or on opening if it has none. Optional exercises do not count towards completing it.

entries.title: Route exercise
entries.body: Route exercises come in several kinds: solve, predict the output, complete a trace, order, break a program, design cases or classify. Solve exercises open an algorithm with the exercise strip and are checked against visible and hidden cases.

entries.title: Specification
entries.body: The illustrated specification describes each language construct with its rule, examples in your profile and links back to the route.

entries.title: Progress
entries.body: The progress dashboard measures coverage with charts: rings for completed lessons, solved exercises and concepts used; the route trail lesson by lesson; the required exercises left in the suggested lesson; progress per level and a radar per exercise kind; weekly activity and your library. It does not measure performance or compare you with others. Exercises solved with the agent's help are shown apart.

entries.title: Settings
entries.body: Settings groups account, language, theme, editor, diagrams, the Nodo agent and contact, and shows the installed version.

entries.title: Account
entries.body: Sign in with Apple, Google or an email link to sync algorithms, exercises and progress. When signing out you can keep or erase local data; you can also delete the account.

entries.title: Language
entries.body: Choose the interface language (system, Spanish or English). Each algorithm's syntax profile is independent of the interface language.

entries.title: Theme
entries.body: Choose a light, dark or system theme.

entries.title: Editor settings
entries.body: Configure the editor's typing assistance, such as completion and construct templates.

entries.title: Diagram settings
entries.body: Choose how the flowchart, the structogram and the class diagram are presented.

entries.title: Contact
entries.body: Write to the PseudoLearn team to report a problem or suggest an improvement.

entries.title: Nodo, the AI assistant
entries.body: The floating button with the node and spark opens Nodo, an AI assistant that sees the screen you are on, explains, checks and runs programs with the engine, and can create or edit algorithms and exercises with your confirmation. In exercises it acts as a tutor: it gives graded hints and only shows the solution after three failed attempts and if you ask. All code it shows is marked Verified or Has errors.

entries.title: Nodo settings
entries.body: Shows the credits you have left, the renewal date, what the last request spent and lets you top up or withdraw consent. The monthly plan brings 300 credits, the 7-day trial brings 40 and 150-credit top-ups do not expire.
